title: feat(runtime)!: /actions calls an action by its namespace or _env (ADR-0150 D5)
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-steve"} -->
_Requested by **Steve** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01FdL1XeUyvVNxLreh3F4Qi9?thread=cmsg_01FdL1XeUyvVNxLreh3F4Qi9Ff4UJdxHJzwSQG7VEko8ou)_

Part of #31691

ADR-0150 child G1, part (b) of three (seat ruling 2026-11-09T12:42Z: (a) `/meta`, merged as #31959; (b) `/actions`, this PR; (c) automation, hooks and connectors). The namespace→package mapping is G2's (#31692, PR #31955), reused, never a second one. Claim by `domain:server#1`, card-thread session_01ADHkmQv69sQL5nfT8xuPWs.

Clause-②: no (narrowing). The addressed paths are new surface: on base they answered `404` ("no declaration", the namespace read as an object name), except through the object-less accident named below. Narrowing, beyond the card's three: a path past three segments is no route on any host, and a first segment that is an installed namespace is that namespace's address (BREAKING below).
Metadata-protocol: none. Nothing an author writes changes.

> [!WARNING]
> **BREAKING**, two narrowings. First-party count: 0 for each. No first-party client sends a path past three segments, and an object segment never equals a namespace (child K's install refusal, both directions).
>
> 1. **A path past three segments is declined (`handled: false`) on every host.**
>    - Mounted host: a four-segment `POST` reaches the domain through the new mount and answers the dispatcher's `404 ROUTE_NOT_FOUND`. Base answered the transport's `404 ENDPOINT_NOT_FOUND`. Five or more segments still reach no mount and keep the transport's answer.
>    - Catch-all host (`createHonoApp`): base read `parts[0..2]` and RAN the call with the tail ignored, and a deeper `_activation` path got that door's shape `400` behind its gates. Now `dispatch()` declines it, and the host answers its own `404`.
>    - A deeper `_activation` path is declined only behind the activation door's two gates, so a caller they refuse gets `403` first. Anonymous callers get `401`. Other verbs on a four-segment path get the domain's `405 Allow: POST`.
> 2. **A first segment that is an installed namespace is that namespace's address** (D5 step 2). The bare door admits an object-less action under any first segment, so on base `POST /actions/crm/log_call` ran a one-holder object-less `log_call` whoever held it, and `/actions/crm/lead/convert` ran an object-less action named `lead` if one existed. Now the first answers the addressed shape `404`, and the second is crm's `convert` on `lead` or a `404` naming the namespace.
>
> FROM a path past three segments TO the three-segment bare path or the addressed path. FROM an object-less call spelled under a namespace TO `/actions/global/:action` or `/actions/<ns>/global/:action`.

<!-- adr-0087: not-required (no-migration-prescription) — carried in the changeset -->

This is a narrowing, so the review of record runs at CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER.

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么：`/actions` 支持 D5 的限定地址。`POST /actions/:ns/:object/:action[/:recordId]` 和 `/actions/:ns/global/:action` 只在该命名空间的包里解析声明，并运行持有者自己的 handler。`_env` 只读环境自己的声明。解析规则和 MCP `run_action` 带 `namespace` 的调用是同一个函数。
- 风险与回滚：两处收窄，第一方调用方都是 0 处受影响。一是超过三段的路径在所有宿主上都不再是路由：挂载宿主上四段路径的 404 换成 dispatcher 自己的 no-route 404；catch-all 宿主（createHonoApp）上，base 会忽略多出的段照样执行，现在改为 404。二是首段为已安装命名空间时按地址读取，base 上借无对象动作“意外”跑通的这类路径现在按命名空间解析。回滚即 revert。

## What changes

- **`packages/runtime/src/domains/actions.ts`**:
  - The first segment is read once, after the engine resolution and before every gate that reads the path. It uses `readNamespacePositionSegment` from `@objectstack/spec/kernel`, in the router's order: a literal, then `_env`, then an installed namespace (`registry.getNamespaceOwners`), else the bare grammar unchanged.
  - An addressed path is stripped to the bare path after its qualifier.
  - An addressed path is two or three segments after its qualifier. One segment answers the door's shape `404`, and so does an addressed `_activation` path, because the activation write has no addressed form.
  - A path past three segments, bare or addressed, is declined (`handled: false`). A deeper `_activation` path is declined by its own door, after its two gates, so a gate never becomes narrower than its route.
  - An addressed call resolves through `resolveAddressedRouteActionDeclaration`. The bare path keeps `resolveRouteActionDeclaration` unchanged.
- **`packages/runtime/src/action-execution.ts`**:
  - `ActionAddressQualifier` is G2's `{ namespace, namespaceOwners }` plus `{ environment: true }`.
  - `resolveActionByName` dispatches on it.
  - The new `resolveEnvironmentActionDeclaration` resolves among the environment's rows only.
  - Both arms share `addressedActionHits`: the holder's object-bound declaration first, then its object-less one. Not found answers `404`, naming the namespace or the environment.
  - `resolveAddressedRouteActionDeclaration` reads the protocol's merged object and action listings, which withhold a disabled package's items, or the metadata service on a host without them. It answers like `resolveRouteActionDeclaration`: a package-scoped refusal becomes `refusal` (409 with candidates), a `404` is rethrown, and anything else is `degraded`.
- **`packages/runtime/src/dispatcher-plugin.ts`**: a new mount, `POST {base}/actions/:ns/:object/:action/:recordId`. It is declared domain-decides-every-verb like its three siblings. The three-segment addressed shapes reach the domain through the existing `:recordId` mount.
- **`packages/runtime/src/route-ledger.ts`**: three rows. The four-segment one is mounted. The two three-segment ones carry `servedBy` the `:recordId` mount, which the live-mount parity gate re-derives. Census regenerated.

## Carry-in: the object-less fallback (G2 review 6743156352, landing note 6743815854)

Settled as **fallback**, in one place (`addressedActionHits`), and read against D3/D5. An addressed call on an object reaches the holder's declaration bound to that object first, then the holder's object-less one. That is what the bare REST call reaches (`resolveRouteActionDeclaration` admits an object-less standalone for a routed object). It is also the order the engine finds a handler in (`actionHandlerObjectKeys`). The address narrows the candidates to one holder and never changes the rule, so it loosens nothing. It is pinned on both doors:
- REST: `/actions/crm/lead/log_call` runs crm's object-less action, as the bare `/actions/lead/log_call` reaches it.
- MCP: `run_action(log_call, { namespace: crm, objectName: lead })` reaches the same declaration. It is the same CALL too: on the fallback the caller's object stays the subject (review 6751465170 ④ 3). The gates judge `lead`, `recordId` is loaded from `lead`, and the handler runs under `lead`, as on REST. This is pinned on both doors by object and record, not only by `packageId`.
- An object-bound declaration of the holder wins over its object-less one.
- CONTROL: MCP's bare arm stays strict and unchanged. `run_action(log_call, { objectName: lead })` answers "not found on object 'lead'". This PR does not move it, because widening the bare MCP arm is a separate decision.

## Known gap, not narrowed here (review ④ 4)

Consider an action that one package declares standalone and binds to an object, where another package's object embeds an action of the same name. That action is not reachable by its address. `collectActionDeclarations` keeps one declaration per `object:name`, whatever package ships it. So `/actions/<its namespace>/<object>/<name>` answers `404`, or reaches that package's object-less declaration of the name if it has one. Keying the collector by package would also narrow the bare door, so it is left to its own card, which the seat files. The changeset names it.

## Verification

Head 791c27239 (round 1 on eef901853; main merged at 39fe3cbc7, after #31959). Every heavy run went under `os-verify-lock`. Round 1 rerun on 791c27239's tree: runtime 576 files, 10642 passed (19 skipped); `tsc --noEmit` clean; dogfood, the `/actions` set plus `route-ledger-live-mount-parity` and the `mcp-*` files, 23 files, 356 passed; `dispatch-gates` 85 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED.

- **New tests**: `domains/actions-addressed-route.test.ts`, 21 tests, on the real dispatcher with a registry double:
  - each holder of a two-holder name is run by its namespace;
  - not-declared answers 404 naming the namespace;
  - two co-owners give 409 naming both;
  - object-bound with a record id;
  - addressed `_activation` answers 404;
  - `_env` own action, and `_env` for a package-only name gives 404;
  - a four-segment non-address path is declined, with an addressed CONTROL;
  - on the catch-all seam (`dispatch()`), a path past three segments, bare or addressed, is declined and runs nothing, with a three-segment CONTROL;
  - an addressed one-segment path answers the shape 404, and more than three are declined, each with a CONTROL;
  - the same call on both doors with a record id: the same object, the record loaded from it and handed to the handler;
  - the carry-in pins above;
  - CONTROL: no installed namespace reads as the bare path.
- **Base arm**: the base answered every addressed path `404` ("Action 'global' on 'hr' has no declaration").
- **Suites** (on the merged head, each `command-exit 0`): runtime 576 files, 10635 passed (19 skipped). Dogfood: the 19 files that exercise `/actions` plus `route-ledger-live-mount-parity`, 287 passed. The whole dogfood package ran on the pre-fix head (441 + 3 skipped files, 3673 passed) with 1 red: `action-activation-door-live` acceptance[1], see below. `tsc --noEmit` is clean for runtime, and eslint is clean on every changed file.
- **The two edited pins**: the runtime pin in `actions-every-verb.hono.integration.test.ts` ("a path no route serves answers the transport's 404") moved from four segments to five, because four is now the addressed mount. The dogfood pin is below.
- **The dogfood red, and the forced dogfood edit**: `POST /actions/_activation/<obj>/<act>/extra` answered the transport's unmatched 404 byte for byte, and with the new mount it reached the activation door's shape 400. The domain now declines it behind the door's gates, so it answers the dispatcher's no-route `404 ROUTE_NOT_FOUND`. The pin asserts that: still no route, and the switch never read. Byte-identity with the transport's body cannot hold, because a mounted handler's error body goes through the one envelope builder (`error-envelope.conformance`). The changeset names it.
- **Gates**: `dispatch-gates --commands` derived 85 families on the merged head. All 85 ran with exit 0. `--ran` reports 85 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN. The changeset gates were rerun on the final commit (`adr-0087-registration`, `changeset-no-major`, `empty-changeset`, `changeset-gate-self-tests`), all exit 0. Earlier rounds found three issues, all fixed: `engine-double-contract` (the double's `findOne` routes through `assertEngineFindOnePredicate`, ledger `--write`), `test-source-alias` (module-top `@objectstack/metadata` in the two edited tests), and `dual-build-cjs-loads` (it needed a full build).

<details><summary>Ablations (each file restored, tree checked unchanged)</summary>

1. Address read off: **8 of 12 red**. Every addressed case answers the base's "no declaration" 404.
2. Fallback off (object-bound only): **2 of 12 red**. Both the REST and the MCP carry-in pins.
3. `_env` filter off (any holder): **1 of 12 red**. `_env` for a package-only name runs the package's action.
4. Addressed `_activation` 404 off: **1 of 12 red**.
5. Package-scoped refusal not mapped: **1 of 12 red**. The co-owner case degrades instead of 409.
6. (On 732c8ae01) the four-segment decline off: **1 of 14 red**.
7. (Round 1) The MCP fallback keeping the caller's object, off: **1 of 21 red** (the same-call pin). The one-segment bound off: **1 of 21 red**. The past-three decline limited to bare paths again: **2 of 21 red** (the addressed decline and the catch-all addressed path).
8. The every-verb integration's new fourth shape and the activation posture gate's "deeper path is still GATED" stay green on the head. The latter went red when the decline sat ahead of the door's gates, and that is why it moved behind them.

</details>

## Review fixes (6751465170, round 1)

- ④ 1: the BREAKING block now covers both hosts. The comments in `actions.ts` and `dispatcher-plugin.ts` say what each host answered before, and a catch-all pin is added.
- ④ 2: an addressed path is two or three segments after its qualifier; both bounds are pinned, each with a CONTROL.
- ④ 3: the MCP fallback keeps the caller's object, pinned on both doors.
- ④ 4: the gap is named above and in the changeset.
- Nits:
  - the `_activation` ledger note now says four mounts and the decline behind the gates;
  - `readMergedItems` is one export in `action-execution.ts`, read by the MCP bridge and this door (the second copy is gone);
  - the second edited pin is named above.
- Settled by the seat: the four-segment answer stays the mount plus `ROUTE_NOT_FOUND`. The names are accepted, and the rows are `server-only`.
